chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, who said:

I wrote to him: May I be your ransom, our companions have narrated from Abi Ja'far and Abi 'Abd Allah عليهما السلام that they said: “When the sun declines, the time of the two salats has entered, except that before them there is supererogatory prayer; if you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it.” And some of your adherents narrated from them: “The time of Zuhr is at two feet from the decline, and the time of 'Asr is at four feet from the decline; if you pray before that, it will not suffice you.” Some of them say: it does suffice, but the merit lies in waiting for the two feet and the four feet. And I wished, may I be your ransom, to know the place of merit in the time. So he wrote: “The two feet and the four feet are both correct.”

And what was narrated does not contradict this report: (990) 27 — Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, who said: Some of our companions wrote to Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام: It has been narrated from your forefathers regarding “one foot, two feet, four, one qamah, two qamahs, your own shadow-length, one cubit, and two cubits.” So he عليه السلام wrote: “Not one foot nor two feet. When the sun declines, the time of the two salats has entered, and before it there is supererogatory prayer, which is eight rak'ahs. If you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it. Then pray Zuhr. When you finish, between Zuhr and 'Asr there is supererogatory prayer, and it is eight rak'ahs. If you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it. Then pray 'Asr.” Because the sense of this report is only that he negated one foot and two feet so that it should not be thought that this is a time outside of which prayer is not permitted; rather, the one who narrated that narrated it in the sense of what is more meritorious. What clarifies what we have said is what he narrated: (991) 28 — Sa'd, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Maymun ibn Yusuf al-Nahhas, from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj, who said: I wrote asking about the times of salat, and he replied: “When the sun declines, then pray your supererogatory prayer, and I prefer that you finish the obligatory prayer while the sun is at two feet. Then pray your supererogatory prayer, and I prefer that you finish 'Asr while the sun is at four feet. If some matter presses you, then begin with the two obligatory prayers and make up the nafilah after them. When dawn rises, then pray the obligatory prayer, then make up afterward whatever you wish.” As for what is contained in the reports we mentioned earlier, that there is no supererogatory prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer, it is to be understood as meaning that there is no supererogatory prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer whose time has become constrained, or during the time of an obligatory prayer in which performing nafilah has not been legislated, according to what we have explained: that when two feet, or one and a half feet, have passed from the decline, then there is no nafilah, and one should begin with the obligatory prayer. On this basis, there is no contradiction between the reports, and what further clarifies that is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ: four feet of shadow-length, indicating a more meritorious timing for 'Asr
key_terms.الْقَدَمَانِ: two feet of shadow-length, indicating a more meritorious timing for Zuhr
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun passed the meridian, marking the beginning of the noon prayer time
key_terms.سُبْحَةٌ: supererogatory prayer performed before or between the obligatory salats
key_terms.وَقْتُ الصَّلَاتَيْنِ: the time of the two salats, meaning Zuhr and 'Asr

ai.seo_question: When does the time of Zuhr and 'Asr begin, and what do the measures of two feet and four feet mean?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the time of Zuhr and 'Asr salat and explains the relation between the beginning of the prayer time at zawal and the more meritorious delay marked by two feet and four feet. It also clarifies the place of supererogatory prayers before and between the obligatory prayers, and reconciles reports by distinguishing between the valid time and the more excellent time.
